title: git review reads are safe and a parallel tool-end keeps the permission wait
intent: A live Build run asked for git_status after Bash had already been granted: the git review tools were declared read-only but were missing from the safe-read dictionary. The same run then failed because Bash settled while git_status waited for the person and the FSM had no tool-end edge from awaiting-user-permission. The wave adds git_status, git_diff and todo_list to safe reads and adds the self edge: one tool of a batch may settle while another still waits for permission. The Paseo provider also carries the Yeah icon.
checks: cd plugin/yeah-provider && npm run typecheck && npm test
objection: The FSM edge proves that the state table accepts a tool-end while the run waits; the edge is deliberately self-preserving and does not say whether every other call in the batch has settled. The scheduler still continues only when all runnable calls settle. The icon is a declarative provider asset; whether the installed Paseo build refreshes its cache for an already-configured local provider is a client-side question.
refuted_by: git_status or git_diff asks although it changes nothing, or a tool-end while another permission waits leaves awaiting-user-permission, or the provider has no Yeah icon
